rows.primary_source: Hugo Duminil-Copin, Lectures on the Ising and Potts models on the hypercubic lattice, arXiv:1707.00520, Conjecture 2, printed p.93 (PDF p.92), https://arxiv.org/pdf/1707.00520
rows.source_quote: Prove that the phase transition of the nearest-neighbor Potts model on Z^d (with d >= 3) is discontinuous for any q >= 3.
rows.definition_source: same PDF printed pp.3-4, Hamiltonian and MAG_beta / beta_c definitions
rows.exact_interpretation: For every integer d>=3 and integer q>=3, on the ferromagnetic nearest-neighbor Z^d q-state Potts model, let beta_c=inf{beta>0: mu^b_beta[sigma_0 dot b]>0}, using the source's simplex-spin normalization and monochromatic b boundary state. The conjectured discontinuity is mu^b_{beta_c}[sigma_0 dot b]>0. In conventional exp(K sum 1_{sigma_x=sigma_y}) normalization, K=q*beta/(q-1).
known_special_cases_in_source: fixed d and sufficiently large q
fixed q>=3 and sufficiently large d
sufficiently spread-out interactions, a different model
rows.reason: 2017 primary conjecture checked. Bounded 2026 literature search found no full proof, but absence from search is not a proof of current open status.

rows.issue: The first appends an undefined q_c(d)=2 equivalence to the integer-q Potts conjecture; the second appends free critical nonpercolation to the wired critical magnetization criterion. Neither appendage occurs in the cited 2017 Conjecture 2 or its MAG definition.
rows.replacement_scope: For each integer q>=3,d>=3, positive monochromatic Potts magnetization at beta_c; current 2026 status UNKNOWN. Free critical nonpercolation is an extra premise for one sufficient route.
